Derived memo metadata comes from the memo payload. It is computed by markdown ExtractAll and RebuildMemoPayload.

RebuildMemoPayload computes the metadata. CreateMemo and UpdateMemo trigger recomputation when content changes. The extraction yields tags and properties such as hasLink, hasCode, and hasTaskList.
I'll trace how memo payload metadata is derived from content and which writes recompute it.

Checking ExtractAll for metadata extraction. RebuildMemoPayload copies only Tags and Property. The MemoPayload proto defines the full property list.

memopayload.Runner.RunOnce is a trigger, though not in production. CreateMemoComment routes through CreateMemo. Location is user-set, not derived. Extracted properties include Title, HasLink, HasCode, HasTaskList, and HasIncompleteTasks. ExtractAll also extracts Mentions, but RebuildMemoPayload does not store them in the payload.

ExtractAll computes mentions from memo content. RebuildMemoPayload stores only Tags and Property in the payload. The exact proto definition and recomputation triggers still need verification.

Mentions are extracted by ExtractAll but not persisted to the payload. The payload itself serves as the derived metadata for lists and previews. It contains tags plus property flags such as title, hasLink, hasCode, hasTaskList, and hasIncompleteTasks. Recomputation is triggered by CreateMemo and by UpdateMemo when content changes. memopayload.Runner.RunOnce rebuilds all payloads but is not wired in production.
Reading the MemoPayload Property message to locate the derived metadata computation.

Derived metadata is extracted during the same pass as mentions, though mentions themselves are not written into the payload. Tags and property fields are the stored derived metadata. The proto comment explicitly states these are the calculated properties from the memo content.

RebuildMemoPayload in server/runner/memopayload/runner.go computes the metadata via markdown.Service.ExtractAll. CreateMemo and UpdateMemo trigger recomputation when content changes. The extraction yields tags plus boolean flags for links, task lists, code blocks, incomplete tasks, and the first H1 title.
